items.claim: The middle step of the row's own onset-escalation argument is byte-false: Moab is not named in the verse where the row says the second person turns onto Moab by name.
items.evidence: The rationale reads the second verse of the span as the point where a rhetorical question turns the second person onto Moab by name. The Moab token stands at two of the span's three verses, the middle verse excepted (sweep: 2 of 3 verses in the span), and the one nation named in that middle verse is Israel, standing as the object of the derision rather than as the addressee: הָיָ֤ה לְךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.48.27, byte). Both Moab sites are the flanking verses (sweep: 2 verses) — the third-person object of the drunkenness imperative in the span's first verse, and the vocative יֹשְׁבֵ֖י מוֹאָ֑ב (oshb:Jer.48.28, byte). The second-person forms in the middle verse are pronominal and suffixal, so the three-rung escalation the row builds (unnamed third party, then Moab named in the second person, then explicit vocative) collapses to two rungs and the stated warrant for holding these three verses as one taunt loses its middle step. Everything else here verifies. All six of the row's quoted runs reach byte tier against their cited verses. The ketiv/qere at the middle verse is real (1 note, single-witness) and is correctly disclosed with the written form set against the read form, and the row does not count or slice across it. The paseq at that same verse is real (1 seg, single-witness) and is correctly disclosed count-only with no intra-verse position asserted. No parashah mark falls anywhere inside the span, so no mark disclosure is owed and the absence is not treated as counterevidence. The three heuristic universals declared as false positives on this row are CONFIRMED as false positives: the flagged exclusivity word is the substring inside the phrase count-only, and the other two are scoped to the splits this unit itself considered rather than to the corpus.

items.claim: The rejected alternative denies any byte-attested new addressee inside the eleven-verse span while the row's own rationale identifies one, and the bytes side with the rationale.
items.evidence: The held-together warrant asserts that none of the internal split candidates reopens the lament frame with a fresh divine-speech formula, a woe, or a new addressee of its own — and it names the direct address to the vine of Sibmah as one of those very candidates. The bytes at that verse carry exactly a new addressee: a second-person feminine singular pronoun followed by a vocative and a second-person feminine singular suffix, אֶבְכֶּה לָּךְ֙ הַגֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה נְטִֽישֹׁתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.48.32, byte), with two further second-person feminine singular suffixes closing the verse, whereas the verse before it is first-person singular speech about Moab in the third person. The third disjunct of the warrant is therefore contradicted at the one site the warrant itself singles out; only the no-fresh-formula and no-woe disjuncts survive the bytes, and both fields cannot stand as written. The cure is to drop the addressee disjunct or to argue why a vocative to a vine is not an addressee change of the class that cuts. The rest of the row is byte-clean: all twelve quoted runs reach byte tier against their cited verses; the closure formula occurs at exactly three verses inside the span and the row engages all three, correctly calling the first medial and correctly holding the verse-final one as corroboration rather than closure because no fresh onset follows it; the single parashah mark in the span sits at its last verse and is disclosed with type, witness and tier; there are no ketiv/qere notes and no paseq segs anywhere in the span, and none is claimed. The four heuristic universals declared as false positives are CONFIRMED — all four are scoped to this unit's own reasoning and none is a corpus claim.

items.claim: The novelty leg of the onset warrant is an undigited exclusivity claim the bytes contradict: the eagle figure is neither unused nor unlike anything before it, and this unit's own second verse recurs at byte tier later in the same nations block.
items.evidence: The rationale opens the unit on an eagle figure it calls unlike anything before it, and the rejected alternative counts an unused eagle figure as one of three grounds outweighing the shared divine speaker. Neither statement carries a digit and both fail the sweep. The eagle noun stands at four verses book-wide by consonantal sweep (4:13, 48:40, 49:16, 49:22 — sweep: 4 verses), so an earlier site precedes this one; the kaf-prefixed comparative stands at three (48:40, 49:16, 49:22 — sweep: 3 verses). Worse for the novelty leg, the span's second verse recurs at the close of the Edom oracle inside this same nations block, in two adjacent runs covering eight of the nine words in that stretch and broken only by the nation name (sweep: 8 of 9 words): וְֽ֠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י and בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כְּלֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה (both spliced from oshb:Jer.48.41) each collate at BYTE tier against oshb:Jer.49.22, and the eagle-and-outspread-wings image is repeated there under a different verb pattern. That is an undisclosed byte-tier recurrence bearing directly on how distinctive this onset is, and it is the recurrence class the campaign requires tier-labelled at write time. A second undigited exclusivity sits in the closing sentence, where the interjection opening the following verse is glossed as not the lexeme used elsewhere in the book; that interjection is attested at eight verses in the byte-swept census (4:13, 4:31, 6:4, 10:19, 13:27, 15:10, 45:3, 48:46 — sweep: 8 verses), so as written the parenthesis is false, and only the fuller formulation given against the other interjection's own cited site is defensible. The onset itself is NOT contested: the verse-initial divine-speech formula is byte-true and divine-mouthed; the preceding verse's setumah is real, correctly typed, witnessed and held at tier-3; the ketiv/qere at the span's fifth verse is real (1 note) and correctly disclosed written-against-read; the exegesis note at that same verse is correctly held as single-witness apparatus rather than text bytes; and the self-magnification inclusio is independently re-collated — the two clauses match at SKELETON tier in both directions and at neither accent-preserving tier, exactly as claimed, and the clause is a two-verse object book-wide (sweep: 2 verses). The three heuristic universals declared as false positives are CONFIRMED, including the tier exclusivity, which the re-collation independently verifies.

items.claim: The closing texture note mis-locates the book's colophon outside the collection this unit declares for itself, when that colophon is the collection's own terminal verse.
items.evidence: The note frames this unit's terminus line as a smaller-scope model of the book's closing colophon, which it places well beyond this collection's own span. The collection this unit declares for itself runs through the very verse carrying that colophon, so the colophon is the collection's last verse rather than anything beyond it — and the two lines are formally kin at the bytes, opening on the identical two words: עַד הֵ֖נָּה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט מוֹאָֽב (oshb:Jer.48.47, byte) beside עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.51.64, byte). Stating the containment correctly would strengthen the terminus argument rather than weaken it, so this is a fix-in-place wording defect and not a boundary dispute. The boundary is NOT contested. The interjection opening the span is byte-true and is genuinely the other lexeme from the one cited against it, which also reaches byte tier at its own cited site. The terminus clause is byte-attested and does close the whole Moab oracle rather than only this unit. The setumah at the closing verse is real, correctly typed, witnessed and held at tier-3. The layout fold at that same verse is real in the staged English layer (1 continuation paragraph) and is correctly held as tier-4 metadata that is evidence in neither direction. Neither verse carries a ketiv/qere note or a paseq seg, and none is claimed. The three heuristic universals declared as false positives are CONFIRMED: the two disclosure words are mandated wording, and the negative recurrence claim against the earlier Egypt-oracle close is true at the bytes — the longest run shared between this verse and either verse of that close is the book-wide divine closure formula alone, with no shared restoration wording.

items.claim: Three byte-false statements, one load-bearing for the rear seam: the divine-title stack does not close the span's last verse, the closure contrast drawn against the second verse is incomplete because that verse carries both formulas, and the stack is mis-counted as a two-site object.
items.evidence: First and load-bearing: the rationale ends the span on a terror pronouncement closing on the divine-title stack. In the bytes that stack sits mid-verse and the verse runs on past it for eight more words, מִכָּל סְבִיבָ֑יִךְ וְנִדַּחְתֶּם֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּ֖ץ לַנֹּדֵֽד (oshb:Jer.49.5, byte), matching “from all who are around you. All of you will be driven completely out, and there will be no one to gather together the fugitives.” (web:Jer.49.5). Both witnesses agree the stack is medial, so no closure formula stands at the rear seam this row cuts. Second, the device note contrasts the perfect-verb tag closing the second verse against the participial formula said to close the last verse. The perfect-verb tag is indeed verse-final there, but that same verse also carries the participial formula mid-verse — נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.49.2, byte), rendered as the first of that verse's two “says Yahweh” tags (web:Jer.49.2) — so the formulas are not distributed one per verse and the stated contrast does not hold at either end. Third, the same note calls the title stack one of two such stacks, naming a second site that lies outside this row's span entirely. The byte-swept census puts the participial adonai-YHWH title stack at four verses (2:19, 2:22, 49:5, 50:31 — sweep: 4 verses), of which three carry the armies element (2:19, 49:5, 50:31 — sweep: 3 verses); under either object definition the digit two is wrong, and the row's own span contains exactly one site. Fourth, the type label calls this a dated nation-header oracle: the header is lamed-initial plus a divine-speech formula and carries no year, reign or date token of any shape, and it is absent from the book's nineteen classified date sites. Fifth, the parashah sentence calls the mark one chapter back the nearest to this span, but a setumah sits one verse past the span's last verse, exactly as near, and that rear-seam mark — the one this row's own cut turns on — goes undisclosed. All three quoted Hebrew runs do reach byte tier against their cited verses and the header splice is correct. The single heuristic universal declared a false positive is REFUTED: it flags the very sentence whose content is wrong.

items.claim: The out-of-span verse carrying the row's entire recurrence evidence is a doubled ketiv/qere verse in which BOTH cited tokens are read-forms standing against different written forms, and the row discloses none of it.
items.evidence: The row rests its restoration-formula claim on a verb-noun pair, quoting it at byte tier from this unit's own verse and asserting the same idiom is read again at a verse in the Elam oracle. That verse is one of the book's twelve doubled ketiv/qere verses (2 notes, single-witness), and both notes ride on precisely the two tokens the claim needs: אשוב אָשִׁ֛יב and שבית שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.39, byte for the full written-plus-read runs as spliced). At that site the verb is a read-form against a different written form and the noun is a read-form against a different written form, so the asserted sameness holds only under the 2 qere readings and is a text-critical claim rather than a plain byte identity; the same verse also carries a paseq seg (1 seg) and a setumah, none of it disclosed. The standing rule is to check the variant inventory before counting or slicing in any such verse, and here the slice is the whole of the evidence. This is a disclosure defect and not a boundary dispute: the one-verse boundary itself verifies — the discourse pivot and the verb-noun pair both reach byte tier at this unit's own verse, that verse carries no variant note and no paseq seg, and the setumah at its close is real, correctly typed, witnessed and held at tier-3. One further gap for the same pass: this unit's own verse closes on the participial divine formula, which the row calls the narrator's tag without ever naming the formula object, so the strongest closure corroboration available to a one-verse unit goes unnamed. No heuristic universals were declared on this row and none is owed.

items.claim: The type label calls an undated header dated, and the internal addressee note asserts direct singular address across a verse that speaks of Esau in the third person in both witnesses.
items.evidence: The type label reads this as a dated nation-header oracle. The header verse is lamed-initial plus a divine-speech formula with the armies element and a rhetorical question about Teman; it carries no year, reign or date token of any shape and is absent from the book's nineteen classified date sites. The label is byte-false, and because the same wrong word recurs on the neighbouring header row it is a factual defect inside convergent phrasing rather than the phrasing itself. Second, the device note has the addressee narrowing from the plural imperative at the span's second verse to Esau addressed in the singular across the last three. The plural-imperative half is byte-supportable. The singular-address half fails at the middle of those three, which is first-person divine speech about Esau in the third person throughout — חָשַׂ֣פְתִּי אֶת עֵשָׂ֗ו גִּלֵּ֨יתִי֙ אֶת מִסְתָּרָ֔יו (oshb:Jer.49.10, byte), continued by third-masculine-singular suffixes to the end of the verse, matching “But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places” (web:Jer.49.10); both witnesses give reference, not address. The span's last verse also sets second-masculine-singular suffixes beside a plural verb, so a flat singular label does not survive its own stated range either, and with no morphology layer staged a form-class claim of this reach should be held rather than asserted. The boundary work is otherwise byte-sound: the header and the flee-imperative both reach byte tier at their cited verses, the mercy clause reaches byte tier at the closing verse, the front-seam setumah and the closing setumah are both real and correctly typed and located, and there are no variant notes and no paseq segs anywhere inside the span. The single heuristic universal declared a false positive is CONFIRMED — it is a hedged reading claim about this unit's own candidates, not a corpus claim.

items.claim: The row places a paseq at a position inside the verse in the same sentence that disclaims any position knowledge, and it assigns to Bozrah a predicate the bytes give to her cities.
items.evidence: The rationale says the cup verse carries a paseq mark later in the verse per the inventory, then adds that the inventory gives no position within the verse. The seg layer is count-only and intra-verse position claims are unsourceable, so the first half of the sentence asserts precisely what the second half says cannot be known; the disclosure object itself is real (1 seg, single-witness) and only the position words need to go. Second, the closing sentence names Bozrah specifically as an astonishment and a perpetual waste. The bytes predicate the four-fold list of Bozrah and reserve the perpetual-wastes phrase for her cities in a separate clause with its own plural verb: וְכָל עָרֶ֥יהָ תִהְיֶ֖ינָה לְחָרְב֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte), matching “All its cities will be perpetual wastes.” (web:Jer.49.13) as against “Bozrah will become an astonishment, a reproach, a waste, and a curse.” (web:Jer.49.13). Both witnesses agree, so the gloss overshoots its splice. The onset is NOT contested: the verse-initial divine-speech formula and the oath formula both reach byte tier at their cited verses, the formula is divine-mouthed, the front-seam setumah is real and correctly located at the preceding verse, and no variant note falls inside the span. Two smaller gaps for the same pass: the closing verse carries the participial divine formula mid-verse inside the quoted oath run and is never named as such, and the signal list records only the speech formula though the row argues an oath formula and a divine title as well. The single heuristic universal declared a false positive is CONFIRMED — it describes this unit's own rejected tiling, not the corpus.
